name: qa_chorus
title: OS-INSFX-FX2 X2, the Stereo Chorus effect module (modules/effects/chorus, kind 2, ABI 1.12, a WIDENS stereo effect) as a track insert from the console: loaded from the card, bound with `diag ins`, heard on headphones, its tail ends at once, and its cost read from the `ins` line (and `diag bench insert`, bench image: its state buffer is too small for this module, see QA-GLB-217). Needs an image with OS-INSFX-ABI2 A4 (the stereo track adapter): before it the OS never calls render_st and the insert is silent. Console only: the insert is NOT saved (S3), and the console has no insert parameter verb, so the Period, Depth, Delay and Mix sweeps and the four factory presets (`ins preset` when the console has it, else the INSERTS page) are a hand check. Needs modules/effects/chorus.tmod on the card (the build's modules/chorus.tmod, copied by the tester). Reset the unit first so that chorus is the only effect module loaded. Writes nothing to the card. Leaves no insert bound

steps.say: OS-INSFX-FX2 X2, rows QA-GLB-214 to 217 of docs/qa/catalogue/global.md (a unit step is named by the row id its note begins with; QA-GLB-215 and 216 are host tests). Put modules/effects/chorus.tmod on the card, reset the unit so that no other effect module is loaded, and open a project with a MONO sample sounding on track 1 (the Dense8 song of OS-DENSE has one). Use headphones. Needs an image with OS-INSFX-ABI2 A4 (the stereo track adapter): before it the OS never calls render_st and the insert is silent. The insert is console-bound: it is lost on save and on reload until the project record lands (slice S3). The default setting is Period 1,667 ms, Depth 40 %, Delay 12 ms, Mix 50 %: track 1 must sound wide, a slow chorus with a different swing in each ear, at the same level as the bypassed track or a little lower (`ins bypass 1 1 on` and `off` to compare), never louder

steps.note: (Shift released, in case a former run left it down)
QA-GLB-214: the packed module passes the loader on the unit

QA-GLB-214: loaded, version 1.0.0; `mod` also says where its hot part runs (the SRAM_L slab or SDRAM): read it against the hot size of the build (the CI build's o3m_pack line, at most 1.5 KB); its 8.4 KB state is over the 4 KiB arena, so it is in SDRAM
QA-GLB-214: bound to track 1, slot 1, with its default parameters; the OS runs it through the stereo adapter (a WIDENS effect)

QA-GLB-217: the insert runs (wet on) and its measured cycles and share of the block are on the line (the spec's budget for a WIDENS insert is 4 points with the adapter [Q4]; the estimate is about 7.5k cycles, 2.9 %): the chorus's own cost figure, since the bench cannot time a state of this size
QA-GLB-217: the load with the insert on; underruns 0; read it against the same project with no insert
QA-GLB-214: nothing was forced to dry

steps.say: QA-GLB-214, by ear on headphones: a mono sample on track 1 has a stereo image (a slow chorus: each ear hears the sound a few ms late, the delays swinging in opposite directions; no zipper, no click) and its LEVEL IS THE SAME as bypassed or a little LOWER, never higher (the mix crossfades the mid: compare with `ins bypass 1 1 on`); the other tracks are unchanged. Then `ins bypass 1 1 on`: the dry sound returns with no click. A mono sum of a USB recording of MAIN is not exactly the dry level (a mild comb: WIDE is the mono-safe widener)

steps.note: QA-GLB-214: bypass is the host's one-block ramp to dry
QA-GLB-214: off resets the module (shutdown, init) and the effect starts from an empty line: no thump
QA-GLB-214: a second and a half after the stop there is no `tail` word: the module returns 0 once the line has delivered its last 33 ms
QA-GLB-214: the render figure is a stopped transport's, with the effect bound and idle

expect: BENCH insert_st \d+ 64 avg \d+ max \d+ \(.*, adapter \d+ cycles \(\d+\.\d%\) peak \d+\)
steps.note: QA-GLB-217: bench image (`-DO3OS_BENCH=ON`, with the stereo adapter of OS-INSFX-ABI2 A4), transport stopped. The bench's state buffer is 512 B (platform/mk66/src/bench.cpp) and the chorus's state is 8.4 KB, so the stereo rows time the built-in identity (the label says `identity`, not Stereo Chorus): they give the ADAPTER's cost, and the chorus's own is the `ins` figure above. If a later image raises the buffer the label reads Stereo Chorus and `insert_st_effect` is render_st() of 64 frames alone (the estimate is about 2.5k cycles)

steps.say: QA-GLB-217: copy the `ins` figures (and the BENCH lines, when the label says Stereo Chorus) into docs/architecture/cpu-budget.md, the OS-INSFX-FX2 CHORUS rows, and into the module's README; over the 4-point budget (10.4k cycles, the adapter included) the slice stops for the maintainer (spec Q4, R1)
